_about: What Knos can do and how far each thing has got. `stage` is the highest of `stages` that has evidence; scripts/capabilities.py checks the evidence (offline, and against devnet with --rpc) and renders the table in README.md. An exercised signature that no document of this repository gives is left out and filled by the release; nothing is `reproduced` until a document links someone else's run. Only a public program id is evidence for `deployed` and `exercised`: the `knos_*` addresses of programs-v2/program_ids.json and upgrade_gate's own `declare_id!`, each listed under `programs` with the version devnet runs there (`on_chain`). A deployment of a build at an address of its own (the 0.3.14 rehearsal's staging programs) is never evidence: what ran there is said in the capability's note, with its transaction, and the capability stays `tested` until a transaction at a public id exercises it. docs/CAPABILITIES.md lists the rehearsal's transactions.

capabilities.what: A statement is compared with its sources (the chain's orders and the GitHub events its receipts name) and lists each deleted, omitted, late or duplicated source as an exception; a resolution is remembered through the memory engine.
capabilities.note: Offline: the sources document is given as a file; nothing reads the chain or GitHub for it yet.

capabilities.what: A payment is booked once and only when final: a retried webhook, a delayed bank status, a transaction dropped before finality or one only processed never makes two or contradictory records.
capabilities.note: A state-machine test matrix (docs/INVARIANTS.md); offline.

capabilities.what: `scripts/secret_scan.py --history` scans every blob ever committed, not only the tree, and reports each hit by kind, never its value.
capabilities.note: Run on 9 Oct 2026 (docs/LAUNCH.md, items 1 and 2).

capabilities.what: `scripts/launch_check.py` checks the twenty pre-launch rows of docs/LAUNCH.md offline: every file and test named exists, no key in the tree, no analytics script, email sender or AI provider client.
capabilities.note: Offline; `--launch-day` fails while any row is partly or not done.

capabilities.what: A missing address on the site shows the site's own 404 page, with a guess at the page meant and the three main links.

tested.names: 404: an address that names no page offers no guess

capabilities.note: Run by tests/test_site_launch.py in headless Chromium on a build of web/.

capabilities.what: When a data file of the site does not load, every page says so in one line with a Reload button: never a blank page or a stack.

tested.names: data: the line is there while stats.json does not load

capabilities.note: Run by tests/test_site_launch.py in headless Chromium, with stats.json blocked.

capabilities.what: The first screen paints and can be used within 3 s at 360 x 740 with the CPU slowed 4x on a slow 4G profile.
capabilities.note: Measured in headless Chromium on a shared 2-CPU machine (docs/perf.json `android`), not on a phone.

capabilities.what: A short privacy and terms page: no cookies, no third-party request, nothing stored by the site; devnet test software, MIT, no warranty.
capabilities.note: No lawyer has read it (docs/REGULATION.md).

capabilities.what: A shared link of the site carries its title, description, canonical address, Open Graph and X card tags and a 1200 x 630 card drawn from the brand.
capabilities.note: Checked on the files; no preview service was asked.

capabilities.what: Each signed transaction is sent to the configured endpoint and any second one, again every 2 s until one takes it, and confirmed by its signature status in one request for all the process waits on; a lost answer is never taken as a refusal.
capabilities.note: 40 of 40 on a stand-in devnet that drops answers as devnet did; forty transactions waiting ask one status request a poll, not forty. Devnet, public ids, own wallets: burst 22/40 on 9 Oct before the fan-out; 40/40 on 10 Oct with it (0 failures, 73 retries, p50 580.75 s, n=40). A first run on 10 Oct with the fan-out as it was before this fix (each transaction's status asked every 0.5 s) had every status request answered HTTP 429 and was stopped at 11/40 (docs/LOAD.md).

capabilities.what: The grace round reads a refund someone else (the relay) sent first and passes with it noted, instead of failing because the order is gone.
capabilities.note: Not exercised: the release runs the round on devnet.

capabilities.what: `knos reproduce --verify` checks a stranger's signed reproduction offline against GitHub's keys (run URL, artifact or token file), and scripts/reproductions.py lists verified ones by owner, Knos's own excluded.
capabilities.note: 0 reproductions recorded: nobody outside has run the workflow yet.

capabilities.what: A Node program with no dependency reads a Knos receipt or statement and the chain and decides alone whether an order is paid, by which transaction and under which terms hash, from the published schema and the IDL.
capabilities.note: Tested on recorded devnet answers; no run against devnet recorded, and no outsider has used it. It reads version 1 transactions, which Knos's relay sends, and version 0 with address lookup tables.

capabilities.what: `knos statement export --to xero|quickbooks|netsuite|csv` writes the bill-import file of each system, one bill per agreed line with its four steps and assurance, and disputed or owed lines on a held sheet, never in the payable.
capabilities.note: A file export, never imported into any product; Xero's columns were read in a published guide, not on Xero's own page.

capabilities.what: The pilot's fair test is fixed before it starts: `scripts/pilot_plan.py assign` draws each task into one of two groups from a published seed, in even blocks, and prints the file's sha256; `power` says how many tasks each group needs.
capabilities.note: A plan on paper (docs/PILOT.md): no pilot has run, no buyer has seen it, and nobody outside has agreed to run the analysis again.

capabilities.what: By default a pull request that edits the files that judge it (.github/** and .knos/**) is refused, however its checks ended.
capabilities.note: As before this release: every bounty and order has had it; a test now holds it as the default.

capabilities.what: Off chain, each deliverable pays the Acceptance price in force on the day its order was funded, and a price rise needs 90 days' notice; 0.20% applies only to the part of a month above 1,000,000.
capabilities.note: The book has one price so far. The 90 days are a term Knos would write into each contract; none is signed, and the program cannot enforce them.

capabilities.what: A default warranty window for new work orders: 10% kept back for 14 days unless the comment or the policy says otherwise.
capabilities.note: NOT wired into flow.py in this release, so no order gets it: the default 10% / 14-day holdback would change what public rounds and plain orders pay. Funding still holds nothing back unless the comment or .knos/policy.yml asks. tests/test_terms_defaults.py checks the function alone.

capabilities.what: The site's numbers read each program's whole history, a page of 1,000 transactions at a time, and say when a bound stopped them.
capabilities.note: Tested with a stand-in cluster of 2,500 transactions. The site's build keeps what it read in the Actions cache, so the next build reads only what is new. Not yet run in the build on GitHub.

capabilities.what: The Agent PR Index scan fits GitHub's own token: it reads only what is new, stops before the hourly limit, and goes on at the next run.
capabilities.note: Tested with a stand-in GitHub that runs out of requests. Not yet run on GitHub.

capabilities.what: `knos receipt verify` answers within a set time, or says in one line why it could not.
capabilities.note: Tested with a stand-in cluster and a stand-in clock.

capabilities.what: The date the workflows install from PyPI up to is written from the time PyPI took the release's wheel, so those jobs can see that release.
capabilities.note: The cutoff in this tree was written for 0.3.25. The 0.3.26 release run writes its own after the upload (docs/RELEASE.md).

capabilities.what: Search engines get a title for a person, facts in JSON-LD, a page of questions, a page for the ten-second check, a sitemap and llms.txt.
capabilities.note: Not yet submitted to a search engine: only the founder can do that (docs/SEO.md).

capabilities.what: A result signed outside CI counts only when anyone can check its signature: the Sigstore adapter checks SLSA provenance, the Fulcio certificate and the Rekor inclusion proof against Sigstore's published keys.
capabilities.note: Tested on two real npm records recorded here (knos-settle 0.3.25 and sigstore 3.0.0); no outside source feeds a meter yet (docs/SOURCES.md).

capabilities.what: The self-host bundle signs people in through any OpenID Connect provider (PKCE, ID token checked against its keys), with roles, and logs each approval and export in a hash chain in the memory engine.
capabilities.note: Tested against a stand-in provider only: no real provider has been tried, and the bundle has never been deployed (docs/SELFHOST.md).
